title: Canonical affine-presentation pro-etale derived sections map
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a unital ring, and use ordinary fixed-$\Lambda$ module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $I$ be a small category, $D:I\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$ a diagram and $c$ a cone on its image in $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with vertex $U\to X$ and projections $U\to D(i)$. Let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, let $J^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of fixed-$\Lambda$ module sheaves and let $e:Q(J^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, where $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Define the strict $I^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagram $i\mapsto J^\bullet(D(i))$ by sheaf restriction. The comparison inverse-image unit [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], followed by restriction along the projections, defines its cocone into $(\nu_X^*J^\bullet)(U)$. Define the canonical map from $Q(\varinjlim_{I^{\mathrm{op}}}J^\bullet(D(i)))$ to $R\Gamma(U,\nu_X^*K)$ by applying $Q$ to the cocone-induced colimit map [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], then the right-derived evaluation unit, and finally the identification induced by $e$ and the exact inverse-image localization comparison. Here evaluation is at $U$ on the pro-etale site, equivalently on its slice. Cofilteredness, affineness, the scheme-limit property and bounded-below injectivity are conditions for the continuity theorem, not for defining this canonical map.
